ANTAM supports its decarbonization strategy through robust governance mechanisms and strategic resource acquisition. The company conducts materiality assessments to identify and prioritize critical sustainability issues across economic, environmental, social, and governance areas. All emission control policies comply with government regulations including Presidential Regulation No. 61/2011 on the GHG Reduction Action Plan. To secure long-term resources for clean energy industries, ANTAM acquired the Lililef Sawai and Marimoi I blocks, which will strengthen their nickel reserves while supporting the energy transition by supplying raw materials for clean energy-based industries. strategy_summary:
CIMB Niaga's 2024 decarbonization strategy follows a science-based approach aligned with the Net Zero 2050 ambition, with specific interim targets for 2030. The bank has established a dedicated governance structure comprising the Sustainability Unit and Integrated & Climate Risk Unit to manage climate-related risks and opportunities. The strategy focuses on six carbon-intensive sectors (thermal coal mining, cement, palm oil, power, oil and gas, and real estate), with tailored decarbonization targets for each sector based on the Net Zero Strategy & Climate Risk Management project launched in 2023. As part of the Net Zero Banking Alliance, the bank has committed to achieving net zero GHG emissions across Scope 1, 2, and 3 by 2050, with interim targets for Scope 1 and 2 by 2030.

The bank has implemented several concrete initiatives to reduce emissions, including an Internal Carbon Pricing (ICP) framework that assigns economic value to GHG emissions. Through this framework, they've purchased 11,284 MWh of Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) in 2024, equivalent to 9,817.08 tons of CO2 reduction, and acquired 7,000 technology-based renewable energy carbon units. They've also installed solar panels at their Bintaro Head Office, which became operational in March 2024. Sector-specific actions include phasing out coal financing by 2040 in the power sector, implementing 'No Deforestation, No Peat, No Exploitation' commitments in palm oil, and supporting business diversification for oil and gas debtors toward renewable energy.

To support clients' transition, CIMB Niaga has launched gender-responsive financing programs like the 'Kartini Loan' for women entrepreneurs and integrated sustainability into risk management through Sustainability Due Diligence (SDD) mechanisms. The bank has already reduced Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by more than 12,500 tonnes of CO2 equivalent (32% reduction) compared to 2019 baseline, exceeding their initial target of 25%. They've also submitted Climate Scenario Analysis (CSA) reports to the Financial Services Authority (OJK) and early adopted International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) S1 and S2 in their Sustainability Report to enhance transparency.

The bank has defined specific targets for six priority sectors comprising over 40% of its corporate and commercial banking loan portfolio: Power, Oil & Gas, Real Estate, Steel, Aviation, and Shipping. For Oil & Gas, the bank has committed to not extending project financing to upstream oil and gas projects approved after 2021, while simultaneously supporting carbon capture and storage (CCS) development through financing the Northern Endurance Partnership pipeline and Net Zero Teesside project. For aviation, OCBC acted as sole lender for Cathay Pacific's sustainability-linked loan and executed the industry's first sustainability-linked loan (SLL)-based aircraft portfolio financing. Beyond client financing, OCBC is building internal capacity through its Net-Zero Navigator training sessions in Singapore and a comprehensive Net-Zero Capacity Building Framework with three levels: Foundational Knowledge, Sectoral Deep Dives, and Thematic training. These training programs are specifically designed for relationship managers, product partners, and risk managers across Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, ensuring staff can effectively support client transitions while understanding local market contexts.

The company has established concrete targets to reduce market-based Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 9% from the 2021 baseline by 2024, with a longer-term vision to achieve a 42% reduction by 2030. The strategy integrates climate risk management into business operations through a dedicated Climate Risk Task Force that follows TCFD recommendations, identifying both transition risks (policy, technology, market, reputation) and physical climate risks to inform strategic decisions. By 2024, the company successfully achieved an 89% reduction in emissions compared to the 2021 baseline, largely through the implementation of Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs).

The company has implemented multiple specific initiatives to reduce emissions across its operations. These include using biomass pellets from herbal medicine residue to replace fossil fuels in boilers, installing solar panels as alternative energy sources, and adopting CNG for boiler fuel. Operational efficiency improvements include installing condensate return systems, modifying machine cleaning systems with Plate Heat Exchangers for reverse osmosis, and implementing chilled water systems for space cooling. The company also developed micro-hydro power plants in Sambirata village for cardamom drying and utilizes vegetable waste for biogas production in Manggihan Village. These initiatives contributed to reducing GHG emissions intensity by 85% to 0.057 tCO2e per ton of product in 2024, exceeding the target of reducing intensity by 3% from the 2021 baseline.

To ensure effective implementation, Sido Muncul conducts routine chimney tests to monitor conventional emissions and tracks progress against science-based targets. The company's approach balances alignment with global standards while addressing local environmental needs, demonstrating a comprehensive strategy that addresses both immediate operational changes and long-term climate resilience. strategy_summary:
WIKA's decarbonization strategy for 2024 is systematically integrated into its business operations through a comprehensive ESG framework, with specific focus on renewable energy transition and low carbon solutions. The company has committed to conducting carbon emission baselines and preparing a decarbonization roadmap to reduce operational impacts on the environment, as identified in their 'Room for Improvement' section. This strategy aligns with national policies, particularly the National Energy Policy (KEN) which targets 23% renewable energy by 2025. WIKA's approach is structured around three main pillars: renewable energy adoption, operational efficiency, and responsible environmental management, with specific initiatives designed to address both Scope 1 and 2 emissions.

The company is implementing several concrete decarbonization initiatives across multiple business areas. WIKA has developed innovative energy-efficient technologies including Electric Water Heater, Smart Water Heater, Aircon Water Heater, and Heat Pump Water Heater, all designed to support carbon emission reduction through optimized energy consumption. The company is actively developing renewable energy projects such as solar panel installations and Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) technologies, while also advancing sustainable mobility through GESITS (an electric motorcycle) and Wika Battery for energy storage. Additionally, WIKA is optimizing its experience in energy infrastructure projects, including work on the Cilacap Coal Fired Power Plant and Grati Combined Cycle Power Plant, while focusing on floating solar power projects and geothermal development to accelerate the energy transition.

To support these initiatives, WIKA has established specific environmental policies including the Biodiversity and Land Restoration Policy (No. Doc. WIKA TFO-KP-01.01) and the HSE Policy (No. Doc. WIKA-HSE-KP-01.01), which emphasizes protecting the environment from project impacts. The company is collaborating with government initiatives to access sustainable financing and pro-energy transition regulations, while developing human capital in the EPCP (Engineering, Procurement, Construction, and Project) field to strengthen decarbonization capabilities. WIKA's decarbonization strategy is further supported by their commitment to waste management, emissions reduction, and biodiversity conservation, demonstrating a systematic approach to reducing environmental impact across all operational aspects.

strategy_summary:
ESSA's decarbonization strategy for 2024 centers on two primary approaches: implementing carbon capture technology in ammonia production and optimizing energy efficiency across operations. The company has identified energy management as a material topic in its 2024 Sustainability Report, recognizing it as crucial for reducing emissions while maintaining operational competitiveness in LPG, Condensate, and Ammonia production. ESSA's approach integrates regulatory compliance with business resilience, positioning decarbonization as both an environmental necessity and strategic business advantage in the evolving global energy landscape.

The cornerstone of ESSA's decarbonization efforts is the Low-Carbon Ammonia Innovation Project, which aims to capture and store carbon dioxide from ammonia production. This initiative targets approximately 2,547 tons of CO₂ per day (0.9 million tons annually), representing about 69% of total emissions from the Panggai Ammonia Plant (PAU). The project follows a structured three-phase implementation: the completed GHG Measurement Study by JGC Corporation and JOGMEC; the ongoing Subsurface Study by LAPI ITB (target completion February 2025); and the Surface Facility Study, also led by LAPI ITB, with completion targeted by end of 2024. The project, initiated in 2021, is progressing toward commissioning in Q4 2027 and positions ESSA as a leader in advancing Carbon Capture and Storage technology within Indonesia's ammonia industry.

To complement its carbon capture initiative, ESSA has committed to a 1% energy conservation reduction over the next five years. The company implements this through periodic energy audits, systematic conservation programs, adoption of energy-efficient technologies, and integration of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)-based efficiency calculations. This energy efficiency strategy serves as both a risk mitigation approach against energy cost fluctuations and a contributor to environmental sustainability by lowering carbon emissions. ESSA's decarbonization approach demonstrates a practical implementation of sustainability principles, focusing on tangible technological innovation that minimizes environmental impact without compromising productivity.

The company's approach specifically focuses on compensating for residual emissions from energy, industrial processes and product use (IPPU), and Forestry and Other Land Use (FOLU) sectors through carbon offset scenarios. This strategic framework aligns with Indonesia's national policies, particularly Minister of Environment and Forestry Regulation (KepmenLHK) 169/2022, which outlines the Operational Plan for Indonesia's FOLU Net Sink 2030 for climate change mitigation and the Indonesia Long-Term Strategy for Low Carbon and Climate Resilience (LTS-LCCR) 2050.

For the longer term, by 2060, emissions are projected to decline to 55.3 thousand tons CO2e under the NZE1 scenario, while the NZE2 scenario envisions using 100% zero-emission electricity from renewable energy sources including nuclear power.

To support this transition, the company is implementing carbon sequestration measures and conducting analysis of various mitigation action scenarios. The decarbonization roadmap is designed to transform the mining business cycle toward achieving a net-negative emissions target (net sinker). The strategy includes specific initiatives such as utilizing biofuels and biomass as alternative fuels to reduce emissions, with the ultimate goal of enabling the realization of both FOLU Net Sink 2030 and NZE 2060 policy targets within the company's jurisdiction.

strategy_summary:
PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) has established a comprehensive decarbonization strategy centered on its commitment to achieving net zero emissions by 2050, with a validated near-term target for 2030. This strategy, validated by the Science-Based Target Initiative (SBTI) in 2024, makes BRI the first financial institution in Indonesia to have its near-term net zero target approved by SBTi. The bank's approach integrates climate risk into its core financing operations while aligning with Indonesia's national climate goals, including the country's Net Zero Emissions (NZE) target of 2060. BRI's strategy focuses on both reducing its operational emissions and influencing its portfolio emissions through sustainable finance mechanisms, with particular emphasis on the banking sector's role in facilitating the transition to a low-carbon economy.

BRI has implemented several concrete initiatives to advance its decarbonization goals. The bank utilizes the Sectoral Decarbonization Approach (SDA) to establish emission reduction targets for each industry sector based on carbon intensity, while employing the Temperature Rating Method (TRA) to evaluate and reduce the temperature score of its financing portfolio. BRI is targeting a temperature rating of 1.75°C for Scope 1 & 2 emissions and 2.0°C for Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions. The bank has issued a Green Bond worth IDR 2.5 Trillion and a Social Loan worth USD 800 Million in 2024, while also publishing specific financing policies for high-emission sectors like oil, gas, and coal. Operationally, BRI has installed solar panels at 143 work units and operates 796 eco-friendly vehicles through its Green Network Initiative framework.

To support these initiatives, BRI has incorporated climate risk into its financing considerations through Negative List Policy, Sub-Sector Financing Policies, and Sustainability-Linked Loans. The bank conducts Climate Risk Stress Testing (CRST) in two phases to assess portfolio resilience and has established Credit Risk Rating (CRR) and Credit Risk Scoring (CRS) methodologies that account for climate considerations. BRI actively participates in climate change policy evaluations through industry associations like PERBANAS and the Science Based Targets initiative, while also benefiting from lower interest rates on ESG-based funding compared to conventional financing. This multi-faceted approach demonstrates BRI's commitment to both reducing its own carbon footprint and facilitating the broader transition to a sustainable financial system in Indonesia.
